name: 386 (IBM-made)
yearNote: Introduction year from discovery catalog; not independently verified for this mask.
specimenDescription:
IBM 51F1784ESD 386 die
Metal-capped, 132-pin module
The measured physical size of the die is 11.5 mm × 11.7 mm, but the approximate usable area is smaller, similar to the i386 manufactured in the CHMOS III process, ca. 104 mm².

Intel licensed the i386 design to third parties. IBM was granted the right to produce some Intel 386s for its own use. IBM used the C4 (Controlled Collapse Chip Connection), an early flip-chip technique where the die was mounted upside down and soldered directly to the substrate, all mounted in a metal case to protect the die and help with thermal dissipation.

name: R3051/R3052
yearNote: Introduction year from discovery catalog; not independently verified for this mask.
specimenDescription:
The IDT IDT79R3051 family is a series of high-performance 32-bit microprocessors featuring a high level of integration which are targeted to high-performance, but cost sensitive embedded processing applications. The IDT79R3051 family is designed to bring the high-performance inherent in the MIPS RISC architecture into low-cost, simplified, power sensitive applications.
Functional units were integrated onto the CPU core in order to reduce the total system cost, without significantly degrading system performance. Thus, the IDT79R3051 family is able to offer 35MIPS of integer performance at 40MHz without requiring external SRAM or caches. Furthermore, the IDT79R3051 family brings dramatic power reduction to these embedded applications, allowing the use of low-cost packaging for devices up to 25 MHz. The IDT79R3051 family allows customer applications to bring maximum performance at minimum cost.
The IDT79R3051 family could be viewed as the embodiment of a discrete solution built around the IDT79R3000A or IDT79R3001. However, by integrating this functionality on a single chip, dramatic cost and power reductions are achieved.
The IDT79R3052"E" incorporates 8kB of Instruction Cache, and features a full-function Memory Management Unit (MMU), including a 64-entry fully-associative Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB). This is the same MMU incorporated into the IDT79R3000A and IDT79R3001.

Die size: 7.0 x 5.2 mm

name: Xeon E7 (Westmere-EX)
yearNote: Introduction year from discovery catalog; not independently verified for this mask.
specimenDescription:
S-SPEC: SLC3W
This is a 10-Core Westmere-EX cpu.
It took the automated system 2hrs and 50mins to collect all 777 photos.
I fixed the auto-focus issue that impacted the previous die-shot of the broadwell cpu.
The issue was that I assumed that the cpus are perfectly flat and that I would only need to correct for levelling issues. In reality, larger chips like this bow enough to cause problems with the focus. I fixed it by swtiching from using a single focus plane with only 3 calibration points to allowing for the collection of extra calibration points and creating a triangular mesh between them.

(Flickr wasn't letting me upload a copy with more than 14.9K pixels wide, sorry)
